saints.name: Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin
saints.title: Married Couple
saints.shortBlurb: The devout parents of St. Thérèse of Lisieux, the first spouses canonized together as a couple…
biography: Louis Martin, a watchmaker, and Marie-Azélie (Zélie) Guérin, a lacemaker, married at Alençon in 1858 and built a household of deep faith and daily charity. Of their nine children, four died young; the five daughters who survived all entered religious life, among them the youngest, Thérèse, who became a Carmelite and a Doctor of the Church.

Zélie died of cancer in 1877 while her children were still small, and Louis, after years of devoted fatherhood, suffered a long final illness and died in 1894. They were canonized together by Pope Francis in 2015, the first married couple raised to the altars as spouses.
saints.knownFor: Raising a saintly family and holiness in married life.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin (vatican.va)
